sentences: I wedge the clay on the plaster bat to remove air bubbles before throwing it on the wheel.
I center the clay on the spinning wheel by pressing with both hands until it stops wobbling.
I press my thumbs into the center of the clay to open it into a bowl shape.
I pull the walls of the cylinder upward with my fingers to make them thinner and taller.
I shape the rim of the pot with a damp sponge to create a smooth, even lip.
I trim the foot of the leather-hard pot on the wheel using a loop tool.
I score and slip the handle before attaching it to the side of the mug.
I place the finished pots on a shelf to dry slowly under a plastic sheet.
I load the bisque kiln and set the controller to fire to cone 04.
I measure the glaze ingredients by weight and mix them with water in a bucket.
I dip the bisque-fired bowl into the glaze bucket for three seconds.
I wipe the glaze off the bottom of the pot with a damp sponge.
I place the glazed pots on stilts inside the electric kiln for firing.
I program the kiln to ramp up to cone 6 over eight hours.
I check the kiln peephole to see if the witness cone is bending.
I wait for the kiln to cool to room temperature before opening the lid.
I unload the cooled kiln and inspect each piece for cracks or flaws.
I sand the rough bottom of the fired pot with a diamond pad.
I slake down dried clay scraps in a bucket of water to make new clay.
I clean my throwing tools and sponge after each session at the wheel.
